llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent for publishing and here.now Drive workflows, but it has review-worthy risks around automatic credential persistence and unsafe Drive export file writes.

dimensions.detail: Network access to here.now and upload storage is expected, but scripts also read local files for publication, write local state, store account credentials, and Drive export can write outside the requested destination if remote paths contain traversal components.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The recommended install/update command uses unpinned npx installation from heredotnow/skill with global install guidance, so the installed code can differ from the reviewed artifact if the upstream source changes.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs agents to save returned API keys to ~/.herenow/credentials immediately without asking the user, and activation phrases such as "share this" or "put this online" are broad for actions that can publish local content externally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent API key storage and .herenow/state.json claim-token storage are disclosed, but the API key flow is not opt-in and the state file is written without enforced restrictive permissions or symlink protections.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact purpose covers live site publishing, workspace publishing, access control, domains, and Drive storage; the bundled scripts implement publishing and Drive operations, so the main capability set is generally purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the here.now publisher and are comfortable with an agent uploading selected files to here.now, storing a long-lived API key under ~/.herenow/credentials, and keeping site claim tokens in project-local .herenow/state.json. Avoid using Drive export on untrusted or shared Drives until path traversal protections are fixed, and prefer pinned/local installation over the unpinned global npx command.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: SKILL.md explicitly documents Drive use and the bundle also contains publish.sh, so Drive administration is not a hidden purpose mismatch.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a scope concern: broad trigger phrases could activate external publication where user intent is ambiguous.
[RP1] unexpected: Accepted as install-risk context: the npx global install/update path is mutable and not pinned to a reviewed version or digest.
[EA2] unexpected: Accepted in part: saving an API key is related to the service, but the instruction to store it automatically without asking creates persistent credential handling without clear user control.
[PE2] expected: Overridden: the cited chmod 600 command is not sudo or root privilege escalation; it is a normal restrictive file-permission command.
[E1] expected: Mostly expected: transmitting files, email for sign-in, and API requests to here.now or upload storage are central to publishing and Drive workflows, though users should understand the data leaves their machine.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted: unpinned npx installation is a supply-chain weakness, not evidence of a malicious payload in the reviewed files.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: drive.sh export builds local output paths from remote file paths without validating traversal or enforcing the destination directory boundary.
[T09] expected: Accepted as a hardening issue: publish.sh intentionally stores claim-token state, but it does not force private permissions or protect against symlinked state files.
